properties.name: A session re-measured a finding it had written hours earlier and unclaimed_findings returned NOTHING — the ChangeEvent's CHANGED target was a Component and the observation's subject_id was a Decision, so the two never met
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-24, two days after `unclaimed_findings` shipped (#325).

WHAT HAPPENED: the session measured hydrate cost, wrote `fact:hydrate-cost-is-superlinear-in-edges-and-the-byte-store-is-not-the-bottleneck`, then FIXED the cause and re-measured (8,828 ms -> 909 ms). It recorded `chg:write-buffer-gets-an-index-and-hydrate-drops-tenfold` with a CHANGED edge to `cmp:byte-store`, then asked the question the tool exists to answer.

    unclaimed_findings {"change_event_ids": ["chg:write-buffer-gets-an-index-and-hydrate-drops-tenfold"]}
    -> {"candidates": [], "count": 0, "subjects_examined": 1}

**Nothing.** And the stale finding was one the SAME SESSION had written three hours earlier, about the exact code the change repaired.

🛑 THE MECHANISM: the tool walks from a ChangeEvent's CHANGED subjects to the observations THOSE subjects carry. The change touched `cmp:byte-store` (the component whose code moved). The observation hangs off `dec:idea-a-hosted-tier-of-many-single-writer-tenants` (the decision whose open question the measurement answered). **Both anchorings are correct and defensible, and they are different nodes, so the join never happens.** No typo, no missing ChangeEvent, no missing CHANGED edge — every documented precondition was met.

⭐ WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT LIMIT FROM THE ONES ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. The tool's own documentation names three: work that records no ChangeEvent, one with no CHANGED edges, and an observation whose `subject_id` names a node that does not exist. This is a fourth and it is the commonest shape of all, because **a measurement is naturally filed against the QUESTION it answers, while a change is naturally filed against the CODE it altered.** Those are almost never the same node. The better a session is at anchoring each thing where its reader will find it, the less likely the two ever meet.

⭐ AND `subjects_examined: 1` IS WHAT SAVED IT. The tool's own guidance — *"READ `subjects_examined`: zero means your work touched no anchored ground, which is a different fact from 'nothing was retired'"* — is what prompted the check rather than accepting the empty list. But 1 is not 0, so even that signal read as "asked properly, found nothing". **The finding was closed by human judgement, not by the mechanism**, which is the same failure mode the mechanism was built to end.

⚠️ NOT PROPOSING A FIX, because the obvious ones both have costs worth thinking about: widening the walk to relation edges (ANTICIPATES / HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT / CONTRADICTS) would reach this case and would also re-inflate the shortlist toward the wallpaper the session-sized scoping exists to avoid; and asking the WRITER of an observation to also anchor it to the code would push work onto the moment a measurement is taken, which is where discipline is already thinnest.

📌 BOUNDS: one instance, one design, one session. It is not known how often the two anchorings coincide in practice — that is countable across the graph's existing ChangeEvent/TemporalFact pairs and was not counted here.
